title: QUIC Non-HTTP/3 Interop-Testcase Inventory Verification
verification_method: Workflow review, requirement-home tests, helper dry-run plans, artifact inspection, SpecTrace validation, and Workbench validation.
preconditions: The documented upstream QUIC testcase inventory remains available from quic-interop-runner documentation.
The repository keeps the existing supported subset stable while the inventory/profile slice is drafted.
scope: Verify that the repository can represent every documented non-HTTP/3 upstream QUIC testcase as an explicit inventory/profile cell with a clear classification, while HTTP/3 stays out of scope and no broad interop-readiness claim is implied.
procedure: Review the upstream QUIC testcase documentation and confirm the documented non-HTTP/3 suite is the inventory source.
Confirm the new requirement and architecture define explicit classes for supported, intentionally unsupported, prerequisite-blocked, and non-mappable cells.
Confirm HTTP/3 remains excluded from the inventory/profile.
Confirm the helper/workflow surface can emit or plan per-cell artifact retention for the inventoried cases without silently collapsing them into generic unsupported fallthrough.
Run the requirement-home tests and helper script tests tied to the inventory/profile slice.
Run SpecTrace core validation and Workbench core validation.
expected_result: The repository has a canonical non-HTTP/3 testcase inventory/profile that makes the broader upstream QUIC suite visible and classed without widening the support promise, while HTTP/3 remains out of scope.
status_summary: The helper now accepts the documented non-HTTP/3 inventory and emits per-run inventory artifacts. The dry-run proof keeps versionnegotiation, chacha20, keyupdate, resumption, and zerortt green while explicitly classifying v2, rebind-port, rebind-addr, and connectionmigration as prerequisite-blocked. Chacha20 now has runnable harness dispatch branches and targeted unit plus process coverage, and a local quic-go/quic-go runner attempt under artifacts/interop-runner/20260513-011027614-both-quic-go/runner-report.json recorded `result: succeeded`, so helper inventory or preflight cipher selection alone is no longer support evidence because the lane now has preserved live proof. Zerortt is also green on the dedicated hosted Linux proof lane, with server-role dispatch, buffered request-line reads, and packet-analysis evidence under artifacts/hosted-interop/25608915721-zerortt-server-proof/interop-runner-server-zerortt-quic-go-25608915721/ and artifacts/hosted-interop/25617834482-zerortt-server-proof/interop-runner-server-zerortt-quic-go-25617834482/; the inventory classifier now treats it as supported/executed. The server-role harness path enables managed resumption tickets plus server early-data admission for runner-driven zerortt attempts, and the manual hosted workflow exposes an advisory `zerortt-server-proof` profile for Linux evidence collection. A local 2026-05-09 Windows zerortt runner attempt preserved artifacts under artifacts/interop-runner/server-zerortt-quic-go/20260509-114555424-server-nginx/ but failed before Incursa execution because the upstream testcase's 250-character filenames exceeded the Windows temp-path limit. Hosted run `25608915721` on 2026-05-09 preserved explicit inventory and runner artifacts, reached managed server execution, saw quic-go install 0-RTT write keys and send 0-RTT packets on the second connection, and served one runner request stream, but failed with quic-go reporting `0-RTT was rejected` after receiving the server HelloRetryRequest required by the then-current P-256-only crypto floor for quic-go's hybrid/X25519 first-flight key-share offer. REQ-QUIC-CRT-0154 locally proves bounded server first-flight X25519 acceptance for that captured offer. Hosted run `25617591021` on 2026-05-10 moved past the key-share/HRR symptom and exposed a queued-final STREAM+FIN flush failure under transient congestion; commit `e7dece89` fixed that runtime path with focused RFC 9000 stream-send proof. Hosted run `25617834482` on 2026-05-10 reached managed response/download success, with the client exiting 0 and downloaded-file checking succeeding, but runner packet analysis still failed with `0-RTT size: 10618`, `1-RTT size: 16499`, and `Client sent too much data in 1-RTT packets.` Resumption source-level managed-server ticket issuance and PSK acceptance are implemented under REQ-QUIC-CRT-0150 and REQ-QUIC-CRT-0151, and the harness now emits opt-in managed SSLKEYLOGFILE traffic-secret lines. A live 2026-05-09 resumption runner attempt passed with runner report artifacts/interop-runner/20260509-001723585-both-quic-go/runner-report.json recording `result: succeeded`.

supplemental_sections.heading: Deferred Coverage
supplemental_sections.content: HTTP/3 remains out of scope for this inventory/profile slice. Turning blocked or unsupported cells green is separate from making the inventory explicit. The resumption inventory cell is green only for the checked TLS session-resumption runner cell with SSLKEYLOGFILE-backed proof. The next unresolved zerortt prerequisites are full hosted/Linux runner success, client-side 0-RTT request-stream/packet-analysis proof, and harness classification. The internal admission-gate proof, bounded internal early-data runtime proof, hosted partial-stream proof from run `25608915721`, local X25519 proof under REQ-QUIC-CRT-0154, queued-final-stream runtime proof under the RFC 9000 stream-send home, and server-role runner dispatch are necessary but not support evidence by themselves. Chacha20 now has runnable harness dispatch branches and targeted unit coverage for the supported-path gate, but it still needs live runner/platform ChaCha20-Poly1305 proof before the inventory cell can move.
